content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Identify the main sources and types of water pollution
Explain the effects of different pollutants on aquatic ecosystems
Discuss methods to treat and prevent water pollution

occurs when harmful substances contaminate water bodies such as rivers, lakes, and oceans. It affects aquatic life, human health, and the availability of clean drinking water. Understanding the causes and effects of water pollution is essential for protecting this vital resource.
Biological treatment uses bacteria to break down waste
Nitrates from fertilisers dissolve in rainwater
Run off into rivers and lakes
Bacteria decompose dead plants and algae
Not enough oxygen for aquatic life
Without oxygen, different bacteria take over

Excess nutrients (nitrates and phosphates) enter water
Sources include fertiliser runoff and sewage
Nutrients allow algae to multiply quickly
Forms a green layer on water surface
Light is blocked from reaching underwater plants
Bacteria break down dead plants and algae
Dissolved oxygen in water is used up
Explain why heavy metal pollution is particularly dangerous.
Unlike organic pollutants, heavy metals are elements
They cannot be decomposed by bacteria
They persist in the environment indefinitely
Organisms absorb heavy metals from water
The metals accumulate in body tissues
As one organism eats another, metals are passed on
Concentration increases at each level of food chain
Top predators (e.g., large fish, birds) have highest levels
Heavy metals are toxic even at low concentrations
Can cause nervous system damage, cancer, birth defects
Humans eating contaminated fish are at risk
Suggest how agricultural practices could be changed to reduce water pollution.
Plant cover crops to absorb excess nutrients
Store manure properly in covered facilities
Spread at appropriate times (not before rain)
Thinking eutrophication adds oxygen to water
Decomposition of algae REMOVES oxygen from water
Bioaccumulation means build-up in organisms; biodegradation means breakdown
Fertilisers are beneficial; it's EXCESS that causes problems
Sewage, fertilisers, pesticides, industrial waste, oil, plastics
Nutrients → algal bloom → light blocked → decomposition → oxygen depletion → fish death
Don't break down, bioaccumulate, toxic at low levels
Coats wildlife, reduces oxygen, toxic to marine life
Don't biodegrade, ingested by animals, microplastics in food chain
Proper waste treatment, careful fertiliser use, regulations
Sewage treatment plants, filtration, chemical treatment
